L55@P2-3: foundation for agentic data centers. The expansion into siliconproducts provides the ecosystem with greater flexibility in how they build and deploy Arm-based infrastructure — whether
L56@P3: licensing Arm IP, adopting Arm CSS, or deploying Arm-designed silicon.
L57@P3: The Arm AGI CPU delivers:
L58@P3: • Performance: Up to 136 Arm Neoverse V3 cores per CPU, delivering leading performance per core, SoC, blade and
L59@P3: rack*, with 6GB/s memory bandwidth per core at sub-100ns latency.
L60@P3: • Scale: 300-watt TDP with a dedicated core per program thread enables deterministic performance under sustained load,
L61@P3: eliminating throttling and idle threads.
L62@P3: • Efficiency: Supports high-density 1U server chassis’ supporting air-cooled deployments with up to 8,160 cores per rack,
L63@P3: and liquid-cooled systems delivering 45,000+ cores per rack.
L64@P3: These capabilities translate into greater workload density, improved accelerator utilization and more usable compute within
L65@P3: existing power envelopes — critical advantages as AI infrastructure scales. The Arm AGI CPU delivers more than 2x
L66@P3: performance per rack versus x86 CPUs, enabling up to $10B in CAPEX savings per GW of AI data center capacity*.
L67@P3: Broad Ecosystem Support for Arm AGI CPU
L68@P3: Meta serves as the lead partner and co-developer, leveraging Arm AGI CPU to optimize infrastructure for its family of apps and
L69@P3: working alongside Meta’s own custom silicon, called Meta Training and Inference Accelerator (MTIA), enabling more efficient
L70@P3: orchestration in large-scale AI systems. Arm and Meta are committed to collaborating across multiple generations of the Arm
L71@P3: AGI CPU roadmap.
L72@P3: “Delivering AI experiences at global scale demands a robust and adaptable portfolio of custom silicon solutions, purpose-built to
L73@P3: accelerate AI workloads and optimize performance across Meta’s platforms,” said Santosh Janardhan, head of infrastructure,
L74@P3: Meta. “We worked alongside Arm to develop the Arm AGI CPU to deploy an efficient compute platform that significantly
L75@P3: improves our data center performance density and supports a multi-generation roadmap for our evolving AI systems.”
L76@P3: Alongside Meta, Arm has confirmed additional commercial momentum with partners including Cerebras, Cloudflare, F5,
L77@P3: OpenAI, Positron, Rebellions, SAP, and SK Telecom. These customers will deploy the Arm AGI CPU for key agentic CPU usecases including accelerator management, control plane processing, and cloud and enterprise-based API, task and application
L78@P3: hosting.
L79@P3: To accelerate this ramp, Arm is partnering with lead OEMs and ODMs including ASRock Rack, Lenovo, Quanta Computer, and
L80@P3: Supermicro, with early systems available now and broader availability expected in the second half of the year.
L81@P3: More than 50 leading companies across hyperscale, cloud, silicon, memory, networking, software, system design and
L82@P3: manufacturing are supporting the expansion of the Arm compute platform into silicon. That momentum includes industry leaders
L83@P3-4: such as AWS, Broadcom,Google, Marvell, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC, alongside many others.
L84@P4: A New Era for the Arm Compute Platform
L85@P4: For decades, the industry has built on the Arm compute platform through its industry-leading IP and, more recently, Arm CSS,
L86@P4: grounded in a foundation of high-performance, power-efficient computing. The expansion into production silicon with the Arm
L87@P4: AGI CPU marks the next phase of that evolution — extending Arm into data center silicon and bringing its power-efficient
L88@P4: architecture to AI infrastructure at scale.
L89@P4: Ecosystem support:
L90@P4: Click here to view supporting quotes from more than 50 leading ecosystem players:
L91@P4: Advantest, Altera, AMI, Amazon Web Services, Amkor, Arista, ASRock Rack, ASE Holdings, Broadcom, Bristol Centre for
L92@P4: Supercomputing, Cadence, Canonical, Cerebras, Cisco, Cloudflare, Databricks, F5, Furiosa, GitHub, Google Cloud, Hugging
L93@P4: Face, Intel Foundry, Lenovo, Marvell, MediaTek, Meta, Micron, Microsoft Azure, MongoDB, NVIDIA, NXP, Open AI (OAI),
L94@P4: Open Compute Project, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Positron, Red Hat, Rebellions, Redis, Samsung, SAP, Siemens, SK
L95@P4: Hynix, SK Telecom, Snowflake, Socionext (SNI), ST Micro, StatsChipPac, SUSE, SuperMicro, Synopsys, TSMC, VMWare.
L96@P4: Supporting quotes include:
L97@P4: AWS
L98@P4: "Back in 2009, I first wrote about Arm becoming the next generation general purpose server CPU. Over the last decade, we've
L99@P4: partnered closely with Arm in building Graviton here at AWS, and it's been a remarkable success - the majority of compute
L100@P4: capacity AWS added to our fleet in 2025 was powered by Graviton. This collaboration has been great for both companies, and
L101@P4: Graviton continues to deliver better price/performance for our customers. Here's to celebrating with Arm and to our continued
L102@P4: partnership delivering big for customers." - James Hamilton, SVP and Distinguished Engineer, Amazon
L103@P4: Broadcom
L104@P4: “As Broadcom builds the world's most capable XPU and networking solutions for hyperscalers at the heart of the AI
L105@P4: transformation, our partnership with Arm has enabled us to move with unmatched intent and speed. By building on Arm’s powerefficient technology leadership, we continue to deliver market-leading innovations that scale the most complex AI infrastructure.
L106@P4: The new Arm AGI CPU will further unlock the Arm ecosystem for a broad range of customers, creating significant new
L107@P4: opportunities for everyone building the future of intelligence on Arm.” - Charlie Kawwas, Ph. D., President, Semiconductor
L108@P4: Solutions Group, Broadcom Inc.
L109@P4: Google
L110@P4: “At Google Cloud, we are committed to delivering compute infrastructure that allows customers to maximize performance,
L111@P4: reduce costs, and meet sustainability goals. Google’s custom Axion CPUs, built on the Arm architecture, provide organizations
L112@P4: with the energy efficiency and scalability required to support modern cloud-native and AI-driven workloads. CPU innovation
L113@P4: with Arm’s new AGI CPU can unlock a new generation of purpose-built compute capabilities across the industry.” - Amin
L114@P4-5: Vahdat, SVP & Chief Technologist, AI Infrastructure, GoogleMarvell
L115@P5: “As AI workloads grow in scale and complexity, advances in compute, connectivity, and data center infrastructure must evolve to
L116@P5: support the insatiable demand for AI. The new AGI CPU provides more options for the Arm ecosystem and broadens the
L117@P5: accessibility of compute to a new set of customers. Marvell brings leadership in custom compute, end-to-end connectivity, and
L118@P5: accelerated infrastructure technologies that power modern data centers, and we are proud to partner with Arm to enable the next
L119@P5: generation of AI infrastructure.” - Matt Murphy, Chairman and CEO, Marvell
L120@P5: Micron
L121@P5: “As AI systems become more autonomous and data‑intensive, performance is no longer defined by compute alone, but by how
L122@P5: efficiently compute and memory work together. That’s why our longstanding partnership with Arm is so important. Today’s
L123@P5: announcement of the Arm AGI CPU is a significant milestone, opening new opportunities for system‑level innovation when
L124@P5: paired with Micron’s leading memory and storage portfolio.” - Sanjay Mehrotra, Chairman, President and CEO, Micron
L125@P5: Technology
L126@P5: Microsoft Azure
L127@P5: “Arm’s AGI CPU and ongoing CSS investments strengthen the Arm ecosystem for the next wave of AI and cloud workloads.
L128@P5: Microsoft's Azure Cobalt family of CPUs, built on Neoverse CSS, is a key part of how we optimize every layer of our stack to
L129@P5: deliver high performance and efficient infrastructure for our customers.” - Rani Borkar, President, Azure Hardware Systems
L130@P5: and Infrastructure, Microsoft
L131@P5: NVIDIA
L132@P5: “Our partnership began nearly two decades ago and since then, Arm’s adaptability has made it possible for us to integrate Arm
L133@P5: across all of our platforms and for all different phases of AI. Together we’re creating one seamless platform, from cloud to edge
L134@P5: to AI factories. We look forward to building the future with Arm.” - Jensen Huang, Founder and CEO of NVIDIA.
L135@P5: Samsung
L136@P5: “As AI workloads rise, performance gains will increasingly depend on tight co-optimization across logic, memory, and advanced
L137@P5: packaging technologies. Samsung's broad semiconductor capabilities and long-term collaboration with compute leaders like Arm
L138@P5: position us to support next-generation AI platforms at scale. Purpose-built AI compute platforms like the Arm AGI CPU create
L139@P5: new opportunities for deeper collaboration across silicon design, memory integration, and manufacturing innovation with cuttingedge process technology, making this an important milestone for the ecosystem.” - Young Hyun Jun, Vice Chairman and CEO
L140@P5: of Samsung Electronics
L141@P5: SK Hynix
L142@P5: “SK Hynix has a long history of collaborating with industry leaders to support high-performance computing and accelerate
L143@P5: innovation for global customers. As AI datacenters evolve, platforms designed for AI workloads must be supported by advanced
L144@P5: memory technologies that deliver the capacity and bandwidth required for modern applications. The introduction of purpose-built
L145@P5-6: AI compute with the Arm AGI CPU is an important milestone for the ecosystem, and we lookforward to continued partnership with Arm to advance the next generation of AI-driven infrastructure.” - Noh-Jung Kwak,
L146@P6: CEO, SK Hynix
L147@P6: TSMC
L148@P6: "Datacenter AI workloads are evolving, and we are seeing more demand than ever for efficient, scalable compute, driving deeper
L149@P6: collaboration across every layer of the ecosystem—from silicon design to manufacturing innovation. As the Arm AGI CPU
L150@P6: manufacturer, we are excited to support this breakthrough platform. By leveraging our advanced 3nm process technology, the
L151@P6: new Arm AGI CPU delivers significant performance and energy efficiency and is expected to play an important role in enabling
L152@P6: the next generation of AI infrastructure across the datacenter ecosystem." - Dr. Kevin Zhang, SVP and Deputy Co-COO at
L153@P6: TSMC
L154@P6: About Arm
L155@P6: Arm is the industry’s highest-performing and most power-efficient compute platform with unmatched scale that touches 100
L156@P6: percent of the connected global population. To meet the insatiable demand for compute, Arm is delivering advanced solutions
L157@P6: that allow the world’s leading technology companies to unleash the unprecedented experiences and capabilities of AI. Together
L158@P6: with the world’s largest computing ecosystem and 22 million software developers, we are building the future of AI on Arm.
